name: Venera 13
best_known_for: First colour images of the Venusian surface — survived 127 minutes in 457 °C / 89-bar conditions on the surface of Venus, twice the original 32-minute design life
credit: Soviet Venus lander pair (with Venera 14). Launched 1981-10-30 on a Proton-K / D-1 from Baikonur. Venus arrival 1982-03-01: the 1645 kg titanium descent capsule separated from the flyby bus, entered the atmosphere at 11.2 km/s, deployed a parachute through the upper haze, then jettisoned the chute at 47 km and free-fell through the lower atmosphere with a disc-brake for terminal descent. Surface touchdown at 7.5°S, 303°E (Phoebe Regio, Beta Regio volcanic flank) at 7.4 m/s. First panoramic colour images of the Venusian surface; first X-ray fluorescence soil-composition analysis (basaltic, similar to terrestrial ocean-floor leucite basalt); first acoustic recordings from another planet (microphone picked up wind + impact sounds). The lander operated 127 minutes — far beyond the 32-minute design life — before silicon-electronic failure in the 457 °C, 89-atmosphere CO₂ environment.
